noteKo.usage: accommodate growth/demand 형태로 자주 쓰이며 make room for보다 격식 있다.

paragraphs: Irish Rail is planning a new train line from Dublin to Navan. Now it has made a small change to the plan. The change makes room for a third station in Navan later.
The new line will be 34 kilometres long. It will start at M3 Parkway and end in Navan. There will be four new stations. Two of them will be in Navan.
The third Navan station is called Navan South. It is not part of the plan now. But the tracks will be built so the station can be added later.
Trains will go straight from Navan to Dublin Connolly. The trip will take about one hour. At busy times, a train will come every 15 minutes.
People can give their views on the plan until 10 December. Work may start in 2030 or 2031. The line could cost up to €3 billion.

paragraphs: Irish Rail has changed its plans for the new railway to Navan in County Meath. The change will make it possible to build a third station in the town in the future.

The planned line is 34 kilometres long and will run from M3 Parkway to Navan. It will be electric and have four stations: one near Dunshaughlin, one near Kilmessan and two in Navan, called Navan Central and Navan North.
A station called Navan South is not included in the current project. However, Irish Rail has moved the track slightly so that platforms can be added later without big changes.
DART trains will travel directly from Navan to Dublin Connolly in about 60 minutes. At peak times there could be a train every 15 minutes, carrying up to 4,400 passengers an hour in each direction.

A second public consultation is open until 10 December, with local events and an online meeting on 1 December. Irish Rail hopes to ask for planning approval in 2028, and building could start around 2030. The National Transport Authority says the line could cost up to €3 billion.

paragraphs: Irish Rail has adjusted its plans for the long-awaited Dublin–Navan railway so that a third station could be built in Navan at a later stage.
The proposed 34km electrified line would extend the existing route from M3 Parkway to Navan, with four new stations: west of Dunshaughlin, west of Kilmessan, Navan Central and Navan North.

A possible Navan South station has been excluded from the current scheme. Nevertheless, engineers have altered the track alignment in the south of the town so that platforms could be added in future without major redesign.

Under the plan, direct DART services would run from Navan to Dublin Connolly in around an hour, with trains every 15 minutes at peak times. The line could carry 4,400 passengers per hour in each direction.

Following a consultation earlier this year, the preferred route has changed only slightly. A second round of consultation runs until 10 December. Irish Rail aims to apply for a railway order in 2028, with construction expected to begin in 2030 or 2031 and costs estimated at up to €3 billion.

規劃中的34公里電氣化路線將把現有路線從M3 Parkway延伸到納文，並設四座新車站：鄧肖克林以西、基爾梅山以西、納文中央站和納文北站。

愛爾蘭鐵路計畫在2028年申請鐵路興建令，預計2030或2031年動工，成本估計最高30億歐元。

paragraphs: Irish Rail has quietly reworked its blueprint for the Dublin–Navan railway, leaving the door open for a third station in the Meath town once the main scheme is complete.

The 34km electrified extension would branch out from M3 Parkway, serving four new stops: one west of Dunshaughlin, another west of Kilmessan, and two in Navan itself, designated Navan Central and Navan North.

Although a Navan South station has been explicitly omitted from the project, planners have modified the alignment of the track on the town's southern fringe. This means platforms could be slotted in subsequently without costly realignment.

Commuters are promised direct DART services to Dublin Connolly, with a journey time of roughly an hour and a train every quarter of an hour at peak periods. Capacity would reach 4,400 passengers per hour in each direction.

A consultation held over the summer prompted only minor tweaks to the preferred route, and a second round remains open until 10 December. Irish Rail intends to lodge a railway order with An Coimisiún Pleanála in 2028, paving the way for construction around 2030, at a projected cost of up to €3 billion.

paragraphs: Irish Rail has revised its proposals for the Dublin–Navan railway in order to accommodate the potential construction of a third station in Navan at a subsequent stage.
The proposed infrastructure comprises a 34km electrified extension from M3 Parkway, incorporating four new stations: west of Dunshaughlin, west of Kilmessan, Navan Central and Navan North.

While a Navan South station has been formally excluded from the current scheme, the track alignment in the southern section of the town has been modified accordingly. Consequently, platforms could be integrated in future without substantial reconfiguration.

The anticipated service would provide direct DART connections to Dublin Connolly, with an estimated journey time of approximately 60 minutes and a frequency of up to four trains per hour during peak periods. Capacity is projected at 4,400 passengers per hour in each direction.

Notably, the preferred route was altered only marginally following public consultation, and a further consultation phase continues until 10 December. Irish Rail anticipates submitting a railway order to An Coimisiún Pleanála in 2028, with construction contingent upon approval and expected around 2030, at an estimated cost of up to €3 billion.
